summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission after bone marrow transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 10%, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, and sarcoidosis, was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea associated with weakness and hypotension. He had recent exposure to grandchildren with a gastrointestinal illness, and his symptoms were consistent with viral gastroenteritis. He was hypovolemic and received cautious fluid resuscitation, along with a dose of IV steroids due to missed oral prednisone. His condition improved rapidly, he tolerated oral intake, and underwent a scheduled hemodialysis session. Blood cultures showed no growth, and stool studies were not performed due to clinical improvement. He was discharged home in stable condition on his baseline 3 liters of oxygen, with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and monitor his weight.
